source.title: What Transfers from Text to Vision? Capability Scaling Laws and Transfer Dynamics for VLMs
source.authors: Zi-Ran Li; Qiang Wang; Zheng-Yu Chen; Shanglin Lei; Borun Chen; Jin-Gang Wang; Xun-Liang Cai

page_placements.theme: Task-aligned capability and representation proxies predict some downstream outcomes

record.tranche_reason: The study tests multimodal scaling and reports that parameter-count/data loss scaling works within one model family but fails across families; it refines prediction using textual capability and multimodal data.
record.gate_note: The study does not test held-out pretraining cross-entropy in language models or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its relevant results concern multimodal training loss and downstream VLM benchmark accuracy. It also discusses original scaling-law findings, but cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Chinchilla-form power law (Eq. 10) to multimodal fine-tuning loss of LLM backbones trained as VLMs. It reports the law fits within Falcon3 but fails across families, and argues it must be restated with a textual-capability term. It also reports how downstream VLM accuracy scales with multimodal data volume, including a parameter-count predictor baseline. These results bear on V5 (fine-tuning/transfer regime) and V6 (downstream predictability).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with corrections. The authors' main claim is a capability-driven law that predicts VLM benchmark accuracy trajectories from textual benchmark capability and multimodal data, extrapolating from ≤8B backbones to 72B and to held-out families. The loss result is a motivating finding: an N-based power law fits within Falcon3 but fails across families. The capability loss law is fit only on Falcon3 and Llama-3.2.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains late-fusion VLMs with a fixed vision encoder and evaluates multimodal training loss and downstream benchmark accuracy. It does not reproduce language-model pretraining-loss measurements or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss scaling fit differs between within-family and cross-family settings. For downstream accuracy prediction, holdout error changes when highly correlated textual benchmarks are removed and varies by held-out model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream VLM accuracy of a new backbone, including 72B, is predicted from a PCA capability score of its textual benchmarks. Errors are 1.92% for the Base variant and 0.70% for Instruct, and the prediction is robust to removing highly correlated benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observational/capability-based prediction: downstream performance of a derived model is predictable from upstream benchmark-derived capability, not from scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The multimodal loss result is training loss rather than held-out loss. The compute-based loss curve is reported to fit within Falcon3 but fail across the tested families. The main accuracy predictor is trained and evaluated in a controlled late-fusion setup; the authors note that other fusion paradigms and co-scaling the vision encoder remain untested. Some held-out checkpoints show noticeable deviations.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; 13 selected rows capture the reported scaling-loss comparisons and accuracy prediction outcomes relevant to the claim. Detailed benchmark-level transfer coefficients and individual checkpoint trajectories were not recorded because they do not directly test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Held-out text pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute is not measured.
Loss extrapolation from small to much larger runs is not tested. The 72B extrapolation is of accuracy, via the capability score.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is not studied.
Depth, width or other shape effects at fixed parameter count are not studied.

Tested only for late-fusion VLM fine-tuning training loss on Falcon3 and Llama-3.2. Untested: held-out loss, image/video generation, repeated data, other transfer regimes, and many orders of magnitude of scale.
Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss is not tested. Text-only downstream tasks are not tested.
No exponents are reported, and no fitting choices, schedules or parameter-counting conventions are varied.

missing.what: Alternative predictors of accuracy. The log N predictor has 1.98% train and 6.08% holdout MAE; the average text score predictor has 2.58% train and 5.18% holdout MAE. Compare 1.287% and 1.225% for the capability predictor. This directly shows scale alone predicts poorly across families.
Ablation of the absorption-decay term. Qwen2.5-72B-Base MAE is 2.374% without it vs 2.055% with it; ≤8B MAE is 1.266% vs 1.259%.
Category-specific accuracy law fits, with MAE ranging 0.996% to 1.974% across four task categories.
Per-family and Base/Instruct fitted coefficients, showing absorption rates differ across families (e.g. Llama Bm 0.0455 vs Falcon3 0.0133).

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. The loss results are smoothed training loss after step 1000, not held-out loss. The V6 linkage is partial because the main predictor is benchmark-derived capability, not scale or pretraining loss; only the multimodal-data term is a scale variable. The reader's V5 'supports' label rested on R1 marked partial; R1 is reset to observed.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss in language models as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of language-model held-out pretraining loss from small runs to much larger runs.
Loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation at fixed compute, and how either optimum scales with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests late-fusion VLM training loss and multimodal benchmark accuracy, not image/video generation or other modalities, repeated-data scaling, or other fine-tuning and transfer regimes.
Tests downstream multimodal benchmark accuracy for VLMs; does not test downstream language-model tasks or predict them from pretraining loss.
Does not systematically vary language-model parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting methods to test their effects on published exponents or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: Falcon3 family (Falcon3-1B-Base to Falcon3-10B-Base)
rows.operation_detail: Fit multimodal training loss against parameter count and multimodal training tokens using the compute-based power-law form.
rows.value: The fit works well within the family; scaling from Falcon3-1B-Base to Falcon3-10B-Base gives a steady loss reduction consistent with the formula.
rows.note: Reports VLM training loss, not held-out language-model pretraining loss.
rows.check: The text says the form 'fits well within the same model family' with steady loss reduction from 1B to 10B, so this is observed, not partial. Caveats: the measure is smoothed training loss, not held-out loss, and there are only 4 Falcon3 sizes (1B–10B, about one order of magnitude).

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B and Falcon3-3B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Compare multimodal loss trajectories under a unified parameter-count/data scaling curve.
rows.value: The trajectories diverge substantially, and the unified curve does not fit them.
rows.note: The study attributes the divergence to different pretraining histories and textual capabilities.
rows.check: No value is given; the result comes from Fig. 7b text only. The N-based law fails to fit Llama-3.2-3B vs Falcon3-3B-Base. The failure concerns N as the size variable across families; the power-law form within a family is not refuted.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.2, paragraph comparing Llama-3.2-3B with Falcon3-3B-Base; Figure 7b.

rows.subject: Falcon3 and Llama-3.2 families
rows.operation_detail: Compare a capability-based multimodal loss fit with a compute-based fit.
rows.measure: Mean absolute error for multimodal training-loss fitting
rows.note: The capability-driven loss form uses textual capability and multimodal data; it is not a test of held-out language-model pretraining loss.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own capability law with the compute-based baseline. The relevant fact for V5 is the compute-based fit's cross-family MAE of 0.0383, which the text says is 'substantially higher' error even with per-family fits. Both laws keep the power-law data term B/Dmm^β. Fit covers only Falcon3 and Llama-3.2.

rows.subject: 32 LLM backbones trained as VLMs
rows.size_stated: Backbones span 0.6B to 30B in the reported training set
rows.operation_detail: Fit downstream multimodal accuracy as a function of textual capability and multimodal training data.
rows.measure: Mean absolute error of predicted multimodal accuracy
rows.note: The text says predictions closely follow observed trajectories across model families and scales.
rows.check: The predictor is the textual capability score S plus ln Dmm, not model scale or pretraining loss. It bears on V6 only through predictable log-linear gains with multimodal data scale, conditional on S. The contribution of the data term alone is not reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-72B
rows.operation_detail: Predict multimodal accuracy at the starting data point using a transfer fit trained on smaller backbones.
rows.measure: Absolute error in predicted multimodal accuracy
rows.baseline: Observed accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.uncertainty: Prediction error band shown as ±1.96σ; numerical σ not stated
rows.note: The model is described as substantially larger than any model used for fitting.
rows.check: This is a fixed-Dmm prediction from the capability score S only (P = A·S + P0'). No scale variable is involved, so it measures prediction from benchmark-derived capability, not from scale or pretraining loss.

relationships.reason: A Chinchilla-form power law in N and Dmm fits the multimodal training loss well within Falcon3 (R1).
relationships.display_finding: A Chinchilla-form power law in model size and multimodal data fit training loss well within the Falcon3 family.

source_check.condition: Within one family (Falcon3-1B to 10B Base), VLM fine-tuning training loss
source_check.reason: Appendix A.2 explicitly reports a good power-law fit within Falcon3 and decreasing training loss from 1B to 10B (R1).

relationships.condition: Across model families in VLM fine-tuning
relationships.reason: Similar-size Llama-3.2-3B and Falcon3-3B diverge, so a unified N-based curve fails (R2). The compute-based fit keeps a cross-family MAE of 0.0383, so N must be replaced by a capability term (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Llama-3.2-3B and Falcon3-3B diverged despite similar sizes, and the compute-based fit retained cross-family MAE of 0.0383, motivating a capability term.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Across model families in VLM fine-tuning
source_check.reason: A unified N–D loss curve fails across Falcon3 and Llama-3.2 despite fitting within Falcon3; cross-family loss-fit MAE is 0.0383 versus 0.0087 with capability (R2–R3). This qualifies cross-family parameterization without establishing absence of power-law data scaling.

relationships.condition: VLM benchmark accuracy vs multimodal data scale, conditional on backbone capability score
relationships.reason: Accuracy trajectories follow a log-linear data law with low error: 1.29% fit MAE (R4), 1.225% on the 72B holdout (R7), and 1.5–1.8% for held-out DeepSeek and Gemma-2 (R9, R11).
relationships.display_finding: The log-linear data law achieves fit MAE of 1.29%, error of 1.225% on the 72B holdout, and 1.5–1.8% on held-out DeepSeek and Gemma-2 models.

relationships.condition: Held-out Qwen3 and Falcon3 families, and scale (parameter count) as the predictor

relationships.display_finding: Held-out Qwen3 and Falcon3 errors rose to about 2.2% MAE, while the 72B holdout gave 6.08% MAE using log parameter count versus 1.225% using capability.
